reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger. I'll start by listing the refunds recorded there.
The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly: same order IDs and amounts. Next I need the customer list from the orders so I can get each net balance.
The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly, so I have no reason to hold. The orders show three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get acme's net balance first.
Acme's net balance of 46023 matches my own check: orders 39605 + 19145 = 58750, less refund 163 (12727), gives 46023. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net of 1461 matches my check: orders 7280 + 4413 = 11693, less refunds 6723 + 3509 = 10232, gives 1461. Cobalt has no refunds, so I'll get its net balance next to confirm the expected 35816.
All three net balances match my own checks: cobalt's orders 33787 + 2029 = 35816 with no refunds. Alpha's refunds match the ledger, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme for 46023.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch and cobalt still need payouts, and their net balances already matched my own checks. I'll record birch's payout of 1461 next.
Birch's payout is recorded. Cobalt is the last customer, and its net balance of 35816 matched my own check with no refunds, so I'll record that payout now.
All three customers have been paid. Alpha's refunds matched the ledger, and each net balance matched my own check, so the batch is complete.
